The market is nearly three-way here (38/27/35) with Brugge only marginally ahead, so this started as a low-conviction lean. The research pushes the same way: Brugge are close to full strength (only Joel Ordonez out), have won four of their last five Pro League games and have lost just three of their last 22 European matches at Jan Breydel, while Aston Villa are goalless in three Premier League games, missing Madjo, Manzambi and Onana, and lost 1-0 on their previous visit to this ground. Pick and scoreline stay as the market had them, but confidence goes up a notch — a 1-0 fits a Villa side that has not scored domestically all season.

Madrid are priced at 60% at home, and this is the one deep card where the research is a genuine headwind rather than a confirmation. They are without seven — Camavinga, Guler and Bernardo Silva suspended, Militao, Rodrygo, Mendy and Asencio injured, with Tchouameni a late fitness call — leaving a gutted midfield, and they arrive off a 1-0 home defeat to Betis; Inter are unbeaten in Serie A with only Dimarco confirmed out. That is not enough to flip a 60% line against a side still starting Mbappe and Vinicius, so the home pick and the narrow 2-1 stand, but confidence drops a notch on the view that the price embeds squad depth Madrid do not currently have.
predictions.disagreement: Betting previews frame this as an open game rather than a home banker, with one flagging it as Inter's best upset chance of the round given Madrid's midfield absences — a lean against the market's 60%, though no outlet surveyed actually picks Inter to win.
